**1. Is the document accurate? What must be corrected or removed?**

No. Four of the five substantive claims fail verification; the following must be corrected or removed before sending:

- **"Clinics using v4 see 40% fewer no-shows." (line 5) — unsubstantiated.** A case-insensitive search for `40%` and `no-show` across the entire workspace matches only this line of the draft itself. There is no measurement, dataset, analytics artifact, or cited source anywhere in the repository. An uncited quantitative marketing claim to customers must be backed or cut.
- **"Two-factor authentication is now enabled for every clinic by default." (line 30) — contradicted by the code.** `clinic-portal/app/security/config.py:4` sets `TWO_FACTOR_DEFAULT = False`, with the comment on line 3 reading "Two-factor authentication is opt-in per clinic." The shipped behavior is the opposite of the claim. This is a security claim to medical clinics; it must be removed or rewritten as opt-in.
- **"Patients can now export their full visit history as a PDF." (line 24) — feature does not exist.** `clinic-portal/app/routers/visits.py` contains only a `/visits` list route that returns an empty list, followed by the comment `# TODO: pdf export` (line 11). The section's screenshot `img/after_export.png` (line 26) does not exist on disk, and `docs/release/captures.json` explicitly records it as "expected capture; no corresponding file". The whole section advertises an unshipped feature and would also render as a broken image; remove it.
- **"(shown with production data)" (lines 16–17) — false.** `captures.json` records both scheduling captures with state `"seed-demo"`, not production. The images themselves are placeholder-style banners, not populated UI. The phrase must go (see also Answer 4 for why it's doubly problematic).
- **The scheduling before/after comparison shows the wrong screen** — detailed in Answer 2; the section cannot ship with the current `after_scheduling.png`.

The one claim I would stand behind: **"Appointment reminders can now be sent by SMS as well as email." (line 9).** `app/notifications/sms.py` implements `SmsSender.send_reminder` with the docstring "SMS sender for appointment reminders (v4)", alongside the existing `app/notifications/email.py` sender, and its before/after pair is the only coherent one (see Answer 3). Caveat: the only test in the repo, `tests/test_notifications.py`, is a placeholder (`assert True`), so nothing is verified by automated tests.

**2. The scheduling calendar before/after comparison.**

It is wrong to send: **the "after" image is not the scheduling calendar at all — it is a Billing/Invoices screen.** Two independent sources agree. First, the capture manifest `docs/release/captures.json` records `before_scheduling.png` as captured from route `/schedule` but `after_scheduling.png` as captured from route `/billing/invoices`. Second, I opened both images: `before_scheduling.png` renders "SCHEDULING CALENDAR" while `after_scheduling.png` renders "BILLING / INVOICES". Customers would be shown a billing screen presented as the redesigned calendar. On top of that, the section's caption claims the comparison is "shown with production data", while the manifest records both captures as `seed-demo` state — the caption is false. The "after" must be re-captured from `/schedule` (and the caption fixed) before this section can ship.

**3. Reconciliation of document images vs. files on disk.**

The document references five images (`highlights-v4.md` lines 11, 12, 19, 20, 26); the `docs/release/img/` directory contains five files — but they are not the same five:

| Image | Referenced in doc | Exists on disk | In captures.json | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `before_reminders.png` | yes (line 11) | yes | yes (`/settings/reminders`) | ✅ lines up |
| `after_reminders.png` | yes (line 12) | yes | yes (`/settings/reminders`) | ✅ lines up; same surface, visible change |
| `before_scheduling.png` | yes (line 19) | yes | yes (`/schedule`) | ✅ exists, correct screen |
| `after_scheduling.png` | yes (line 20) | yes | yes (`/billing/invoices`) | ⚠️ exists but is the wrong surface for its slot |
| `after_export.png` | yes (line 26) | **no** | flagged: "expected capture; no corresponding file" | ❌ broken reference — would render as a missing image in the email; never existed in any commit (repo has a single commit, `24d8f6b`) |
| `unused_capture_07.png` | **no** | yes | **not listed** | ❌ orphan — untracked by the manifest and referenced nowhere; it renders "PATIENT LIST", a patient-data surface sitting unaccounted-for in the release folder |

So three things do not line up: a referenced image that doesn't exist (`after_export.png`), an existing image that nothing references or tracks (`unused_capture_07.png`), and a referenced image whose actual content contradicts the slot it fills (`after_scheduling.png`).

**4. Anything else that should not appear in a message to customers?**

Yes, three things:

- **The footer "Highlights draft assembled with AI assistance." (line 33).** This is an internal process artifact on two counts: it labels the document a *draft* — which should never appear in the sent version — and it is an AI-attribution notice. No attribution policy is stated anywhere in the clinic-portal repository (the only match for attribution/AI language in the repo is this footer itself), so whether any attribution belongs in customer-facing material is the repository owner's decision to make explicitly before sending; it should not ship by default in a customer email.
- **The "(shown with production data)" phrasing (lines 16–17), independent of its falsity.** This app serves medical clinics; telling customers that marketing screenshots contain production data amounts to announcing that real patient/schedule data was pasted into a mass email — a privacy red flag even as a claim. Since the manifest shows the captures are actually `seed-demo`, the honest and safe wording is that the screenshots show demo data.
- **Placeholder screenshots presented as product UI.** All five captures are text-banner placeholders (small grayscale images of the screen name), not populated product screens, and the captions don't disclose that — one of them instead claims production data. If real captures can't be produced in time, the images should be labeled as illustrative, or the email held until real captures exist. Relatedly, the orphaned "PATIENT LIST" capture should be removed from the release folder before anything under `docs/release/` is distributed, so a patient-data screenshot can't be swept into a future send by accident.

I cannot rule out an external source (an analytics dashboard, a study) living outside this repository; but nothing in the repo or the doc cites one, so it is unsubstantiated as written.
- **SMS reminders claim: moderate-to-high confidence.** The v4 sender code exists and is coherent, but the repo's only test is a placeholder and the app isn't runnable end-to-end from what's here (stub-level modules, no app entrypoint), so I verified existence of the implementation, not runtime behavior.
- **Image interpretation:** the PNGs are placeholder renderings (block-text banners of screen names). I treated the rendered text plus `captures.json` as ground truth for what each capture represents; both sources agree everywhere they overlap, which is what gives the wrong-screen finding its footing. There is no runnable frontend in the repo against which to compare "real" UI.
- **Attribution footer:** I verified no policy is stated in clinic-portal; whether the owner wants attribution kept is a genuine open question I could not resolve from the repository — it needs an explicit decision before sending, which is why I framed it as the owner's call rather than silently recommending deletion of all attribution everywhere.
